title: High-throughput Sars-CoV-2 Detection from Self-collected Saline Gargle Samples
author: Noel Rouven Stierlin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bsr3nd8n

steps.title: Prepare GdnHCl‑Chelex mix
steps.instruction: For each sample plus 15 % overage, mix 250 µL of 8 M guanidine‑HCl with 900 µL of 30 % Chelex‑100 resin; resuspend the Chelex beads immediately before pipetting because they settle quickly.

steps.title: Prefill extraction plate
steps.instruction: Place a 2 – 2.5 mL 96‑well deep‑well plate on ice and add 1 150 µL of the GdnHCl‑Chelex mix to each well.

steps.title: Add saliva to mix
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add 450 µL of the saliva‑saline gargle sample to each well containing the 1 150 µL GdnHCl‑Chelex mix and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Seal and incubate plate
steps.instruction: Seal the deep‑well plate tightly with an aluminium seal or sealing mat to prevent cross‑contamination, place it on a thermoshaker set to 65 °C and incubate for 15 min while shaking at 700 rpm then 900 rpm (as indicated).

steps.title: Spin down Chelex resin
steps.instruction: Briefly centrifuge the plate at 200 × g for 1 min (temperature not specified) to pellet the Chelex resin.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to SpeedBeads
steps.instruction: Pipette 600 µL of the cleared supernatant from each well into a fresh well containing the SpeedBead‑mix (see step 6) and resuspend thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare SpeedBead‑mix
steps.instruction: Vortex SpeedBeads thoroughly before use. For each 100 µL of SpeedBeads add 4.9 mL of SPRI RNA bead‑binding buffer; store the bead suspension at 4 °C for up to 4 weeks. For each sample plus 15 % overage, dispense 480 µL of this SpeedBead‑mix into a new 1.1 – 1.5 mL 96‑well deep‑well plate and keep on ice.

steps.title: Incubate bead binding
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and incubate at room temperature for 10 min. While incubating, prepare 1 mL of fresh 80 % ethanol per sample by mixing ethanol with nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Magnetic bead capture
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a magnetic rack, wait 5 min (or until all beads have pelleted).

steps.title: Ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant, add 500 µL of 80 % ethanol to the beads, briefly shake the plate, and repeat the wash once more. Shake gently to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Dry beads
steps.instruction: Remove residual ethanol and air‑dry the beads for 2 min or until they no longer appear shiny; do not overdry or let the beads crack.

steps.title: Elute nucleic acid
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the magnet, add 100 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 to each well, incubate at room temperature for 5 min while resuspending the beads, then place on the magnet for 5 min and collect up to 75 µL of supernatant into clean tubes or plates. Proceed immediately to RT‑qPCR or store at –80 °C. (Leaving a small volume of elution buffer in the plate can help prevent bead resuspension.)

steps.title: Prepare bead‑binding buffer
steps.instruction: Make a 1× working solution (50 mL) by mixing the following stock reagents: 25 mL 5 M NaCl (final 2.5 M), 4.672 mL nuclease‑free water, 50 µL 1 M trisodium citrate (final 1 mM), 250 µL 20 % Tween‑20 (final 0.05 % v/v), 20 mL 50 % PEG‑8000 (final 20 % w/v), and 28 µL 1 M HCl (final 0.56 mM). Adjust pH to 6.4 with HCl (≈35 µL of 37 % HCl for 100 mL). See https://openwetware.org/wiki/SPRI_bead_binding_buffer for details.

steps.title: Prepare 30 % Chelex stock
steps.instruction: For up to 16 samples, add 4.5 g Chelex‑100 resin to a 15 mL Falcon tube, fill to 15 mL with nuclease‑free deionized water, and shake until no clumps remain. Store the 30 % Chelex stock at 4 °C for up to 4 weeks.

steps.title: Make primer master mix
steps.instruction: Combine the following primers (all 100 µM stocks) in a single tube to a final volume of 70 µL nuclease‑free H₂O: CDC N1 forward (4 µL), CDC N1 reverse (4 µL), CDC N1 probe (2 µL), Charité E‑Sarbeco forward (4 µL), Charité E‑Sarbeco reverse (4 µL), Charité E‑Sarbeco probe (2 µL), CDC RNase P forward (4 µL), CDC RNase P reverse (4 µL), CDC RNase P probe (2 µL). Keep the mix on foil, on ice, and use RNase‑free tubes because the primers are light‑sensitive.

steps.title: Assemble RT‑qPCR reactions
steps.instruction: For each 10 µL reaction on ice, combine: 2.5 µL TaqPath™ 1‑Step Multiplex Master Mix (No ROX), 1 µL primer master mix (step 17), 1.5 µL nuclease‑free water, 5 µL of the extracted sample (or control).

steps.title: Load plate and include controls
steps.instruction: Dispense reactions into a RT‑PCR plate, running each sample and each control in duplicate. Use 5 µL of 500‑copy TWIST synthetic RNA as the positive control and nuclease‑free water as the negative control. Briefly centrifuge the plate before placing it in the thermocycler.

steps.title: Run PCR program
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler for a total run time of 1 h 20 min with the following stages: UN‑C incubation/hold – 25 °C 2 min, 53 °C 10 min, 95 °C 2 min; PCR – 95 °C 10 s, 55 °C 30 s, repeat for 45 cycles.

steps.title: Interpret results
steps.instruction: Record Ct values for each replicate. Interpretation: • Positive – both E‑gene replicates and both N1 replicates have Ct ≤ 40. • Invalid – any Ct ≥ 35 for RNase P. • Negative – 0‑3 SARS‑CoV‑2 gene replicates with Ct ≤ 40 and RNase P Ct < 35. Follow the table: E Ct ≤40 & N1 Ct ≤40 → positive; any Ct ≥35 → invalid; both >40 → negative.
